held.summary: A speaker biography published by Arabnet states that Saad Andary served as Second Vice-Governor of the Banque du Liban (the central bank of Lebanon) and lists among his earlier posts Deputy General Manager at BBAC, General Manager at Kuwaiti Interests for Financial Investments and Head of Treasury at Arab Bank, Lebanon. The page gives no dates for any of those posts, the only dated entry being April 2009 to March 2019 for an unrelated board role at the École Supérieure des Affaires, so no date is asserted here for the central bank or the private posts. It also states nothing about the ownership of BBAC, Arab Bank or Kuwaiti Interests for Financial Investments, so on this source both the dating and the ownership are unsettled. Different person and firms from the Riad Salameh / Merrill Lynch record the map already holds for Lebanon; the source is a conference speaker page rather than a primary document.

The record's facts (BBAC, Kuwaiti Interests for Financial Investments, Arab Bank Lebanon, then Banque du Liban Second Vice-Governor) were read by the agent before the page went or while it still served, but nothing readable now states them, so it cannot be filed under rule 1. held.summary: FBC Holdings Limited's own board announcement, signed by the Group Company Secretary and dated 21 December 2023, advises that Dr John Mushayavanhu will step down as Group Chief Executive of FBC Holdings with effect from 31 December 2023 following his appointment as the next Governor of the Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe, and sets out his career inside the group: he joined FBC Bank, then First Banking Corporation, in 1997 as an Executive Director in corporate banking, became Deputy Group Chief Executive and Managing Director of FBC Bank in 2004 and Group Chief Executive in June 2011. The private side is settled on the face of the document, which describes FBC Holdings Limited as a diversified financial services group listed on the Zimbabwe Stock Exchange, that is, listed in its own right rather than a subsidiary of a listed group; the notice names no shareholders and none is claimed here. The notice gives no date for the governorship itself, so none is stated here. Separate from the Zimbabwe record the map already holds, which is John Mangudya moving from CBZ to the governorship in 2014.

held._held_reason: SOURCE URL IS DEAD AND SO IS ITS BEST SUBSTITUTE. fbc.co.zw's own notice (FBC%20APPOINTMENTS_v2_0.pdf) returns 404 with a browser user-agent; the Zimbabwe Stock Exchange's copy at zse.co.zw/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/FBCzw-Notice-of-Board-Appointment.pdf also 404s; the marketscreener copy that does carry the notice text verbatim 403s to every scripted request, so it could not be read here either. The fact is not in doubt and is in many places: Dr John Mushayavanhu stepped down as Group Chief Executive of FBC Holdings with effect from 31 December 2023 on appointment as Governor of the Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe, and FBC's own notice calls the group a diversified financial services group listed on the Zimbabwe Stock Exchange, which is the ownership leg. HELD because no copy could be READ here, not because the record is doubted. Next round: General Notice 410 of 2024 in the Government Gazette for the appointment, and FBC Holdings' own annual report for the directorship and the ZSE listing.

held.kind: statutory arrangement giving the minister a hold over the bank
held.summary: The consolidated Bank of Mauritius Act published on the Bank's own site, headed as Act No. 34 of 2004 of 10 November 2004, makes several of the central bank's core decisions conditional on the finance Minister. Section 5(2)(a) requires the Minister's concurrence for determining the accepted range of inflation; section 36(1) requires the Minister's concurrence for currency design and related matters; section 6(1)(y) requires ministerial approval before the Bank subscribes to or invests in companies promoting economic development; section 6(1)(ab) leaves on-lending terms to regulations made by the Minister after consulting the Governor; section 16(1) has the other Directors appointed by the Minister and section 53B(1)(a) the Review Panel chairperson; and section 10(2) lets the Minister increase paid-up capital from the General Reserve Fund on the Board's recommendation, with capital held solely by Government under section 10(3)(b). The same text also carries independence provisions — section 3(3) that the Bank performs its functions independently subject to the Act, and section 12(3) that the Board 'shall not be subject to the direction or control of any other person or authority' — so this is a mixed arrangement and not a bare power of direction, and that is stated here because the Act states it. The copy read carries no amendment notes against any section, so no amending Act or year can be attributed to any of these provisions, and its own notice says the authoritative text is in the Government Gazette; the file read is the version dated August 2023 in its filename, which is why it is treated as the standing arrangement rather than a repealed one. Distinct from the December 2014 dismissal of Governor Rundheersing Bheenick already on the map (index 140).
held.source_title: Bank of Mauritius Act (consolidated text, August 2023), Bank of Mauritius
held._held_reason: RESTS ON A FETCH SUMMARY, NOT ON PAGE TEXT. The agent said so itself and called it the weakest of its eight. bom.mu refuses raw retrieval (TLS failure, exit 60, twice here as well), so the sections cited in the consolidated Bank of Mauritius Act -- s.5(2)(a), s.36(1), s.6(1)(y), s.16(1), and the countervailing s.3(3) and s.12(3) -- come from prose ABOUT the statute rather than from the statute. Round 74 established that a fetch summary is not evidence, after the summariser was caught inventing ownership words twice in this same round. Holding this record is that rule applied to this round's own output. Next round: the Mauritius Attorney-General's office or a legislation portal that serves the Act as text, then re-file with the section wording quoted.

held.people: Kateryna Rozhkova (Director of the NBU Off-Site Supervision Department for six months in 2009; Director of the Banking Supervision Department 10 June 2015 to 18 January 2016; acting Deputy Governor from 18 January 2016; Deputy Governor from 25 October 2016; First Deputy Governor from 15 June 2018)
held.move: from acting chair of the board of Platinum Bank PJSC, and earlier deputy chair of the board, board member and adviser to the chair at ErsteBank PJSC and deputy chair of the board at Finbank PJSC, to Director of the Banking Supervision Department of the National Bank of Ukraine on 10 June 2015, then acting Deputy Governor (18 January 2016), Deputy Governor (25 October 2016) and First Deputy Governor (15 June 2018)
held.summary: The National Bank of Ukraine's own biography page for its First Deputy Governor lists, before any central bank post, managerial positions in Ukraine's banking system from 1998 and three named bank employers - ErsteBank PJSC, Finbank PJSC and Platinum Bank PJSC, where she was acting chair of the board - and then the NBU supervisory posts with the dates given above. The private side rests on a second source named here, not on the NBU page, which states only the legal form PJSC: the Kyiv Post, 'The Woman Behind Ukraine's Banking Cleanup: Kateryna Rozhkova (Part I)', https://www.kyivpost.com/post/66155, says she came to the NBU 'from a private-sector manager', that 'Before joining the NBU, she led Platinum Bank, the 22nd largest bank by assets in Ukraine in October 2016', that she 'led the bank up to mid-2015', that the bank was owned indirectly by Odesa entrepreneur Borys Kaufman, and that Platinum collapsed in 2017 - a named private owner. All dates above are printed on the NBU page; the 1998 start, the Kaufman ownership and the 2017 collapse come from the Kyiv Post article. The NBU page is a numbered slot URL (?member=10) and was opened on 17 November 2026 and confirmed to serve Rozhkova's own page; it describes the First Deputy Governor post as one she still holds, which this record does not assert, since press reports of her replacement by Serhii Nikolaichuk were returned by the same search.
held.source_title: Financial Stability - Kateryna Rozhkova, First Deputy Governor (National Bank of Ukraine, official biography)
held._held_reason: SOURCE NO LONGER SERVES THE CONTENT. The record cites bank.gov.ua/en/about/structure/details?member=10 and says it was opened and confirmed to serve Rozhkova's own biography, describing the First Deputy Governor post as one she still holds. Independent verification found that URL now serves a page titled 'Член ради' under the NBU Council section carrying her name and nothing else — no biography, no employers, no dates — while ?member=11 serves Sergiy Nikolaychuk as First Deputy Governor, appointed 15 August 2025. So all four NBU dates (10 June 2015, 18 January 2016, 25 October 2016, 15 June 2018) and all three bank employers (ErsteBank PJSC, Finbank PJSC, Platinum Bank PJSC) are unverifiable at the cited URL, and the record itself already recorded that it knew she had been replaced. A numbered-slot URL was never a safe citation for a departed officer. The PRIVATE leg does hold on the Kyiv Post page: 'from a private-sector manager', Platinum Bank as the 22nd largest bank by assets in October 2016, her leading it to mid-2015, Borys Kaufman's indirect ownership, and the 2017 collapse. ALSO MATERIAL AND OMITTED: the same Kyiv Post sentences state that in 2024 Ukraine's Supreme Court ruled Rozhkova and eleven others bore joint civil liability for Platinum Bank's 2017 insolvency and ordered them to pay Hr 1.5 billion, about $35.2 million. On a capture map that is the most material fact on the page about this person and this bank, and it belongs in whatever is filed next — quite possibly on the corruption-cases row rather than this one. Next round: an archive copy of the NBU biography, or the NBU's own appointment releases.
